TITLE: UK leadership hopeful Burnham faces tricky test to return to parliament
PUBLISHED: 2026-05-15T14:20Z
AUTHOR: Sophie Royle (Reuters Ashton-in-Makerfield)

For many in Labour, Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham is their best hope to turn around the governing party's fortunes. But before he can challenge British Prime Minister Keir Starmer, he must return to parliament, and that's not straightforward.

ON THE STREETS OF ASHTON-IN-MAKERFIELD (in the constituency):

ANTHONY MCCORMACK, former miner/retired welder: would back Burnham because he is "right man for the job" and would "100%" make a better prime minister than Starmer. On Starmer: "The man is not a politician, he's middle management."

ALAN BIRCH, retired Labour voter: would rather "get Andy in and see what goes from there". Under Starmer things were "going downhill."

RACHAEL HULSE, aesthetics nurse: her family had always voted Labour "but now, that's completely changed". "Labour don't really have that much of a good rep (reputation) any more." Hopes Reform would win the seat. "It just needs a change, because we seem to be just stuck in the same rut."

ANN GARNER, pensioner: "I think Keir Starmer should be given a chance. We really need to get the country sorted."

KEY FACTS:
- Labour has represented the area in parliament since 1906.
- Reform won all the council seats that were contested in the constituency last week.
- Reform leader Nigel Farage told GB News he would "throw absolutely everything" at the by-election.
- Burnham was a Labour MP before 2017 mayoralty; ran unsuccessfully for the party leadership in 2010 and 2015.
- Burnham's pitch: people in Makerfield "have long supported our party but lost faith in recent times" — "We will change Labour for the better and make it a party you can believe in again."
